tasks.title: Code Quality: Fix All ESLint and TypeScript Errors
tasks.description: Resolve all 18 ESLint errors (including lexical declarations and undefined variables) and 3 TypeScript interface errors in LeadsPage.tsx. Eliminate all 'any' types by creating and applying specific TypeScript interfaces.
tasks.details: 1. Run `npm run lint` to identify all errors. 2. Address `no-undef` and similar errors by ensuring all variables are declared before use. 3. For TypeScript errors in `LeadsPage.tsx`, create or correct interfaces for props and state. 4. Systematically search for `any` types in the codebase and replace them with specific types. For example, if a function handles a lead object, define a `TLead` interface and use it. 5. Install `@types/node` by running `npm install --save-dev @types/node` to provide types for Node.js global and module APIs used in script files.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run lint` and `npx tsc --noEmit`. Both commands must complete with 0 errors. Code reviews should specifically check for the removal of 'any' types.

tasks.title: Implement Chat Message Virtualization with TanStack Virtual
tasks.description: Replace the current basic scrolling implementation in MessageList.tsx with a virtualized list using TanStack Virtual to handle thousands of messages without performance degradation.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual testing: Load a chat with 2000+ mock messages and verify smooth scrolling (60 FPS) with no UI lag. Automated testing (RTL): Render the component with a large dataset and assert that only a small subset of DOM nodes corresponding to the virtualized items are present.

tasks.title: Expand Test Coverage for Core AI Functions
tasks.description: Write comprehensive unit tests for the core AI logic, including prompt generation in `prompt-manager.ts`, response validation, and phase detection functions.
tasks.details: Using Vitest, create test files for each core AI utility. For `prompt-manager.ts`, test that prompts are constructed correctly based on different inputs. For response validation, test the scoring system with mock valid and invalid AI responses. Use `vi.mock` to mock external dependencies like database calls or API fetches to the Gemini API. Aim for at least 80% line coverage on these critical files.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run test -- --coverage`. Verify that coverage for `prompt-manager.ts` and other AI-related utility files meets or exceeds the 80% target. Ensure all test cases, including edge cases, pass successfully.

tasks.title: Enhance Dynamic AI Prompt Construction
tasks.description: Enhance the existing `prompt-manager.ts` to support more dynamic prompt construction, allowing for conditional inclusion of prompt sections based on conversation context or lead data.
tasks.details: Refactor the functions within `prompt-manager.ts`. Instead of static string concatenation, build prompts from a structured object or an array of prompt components. This allows for logic to be applied before joining the final prompt string. For example: `const promptParts = [baseIntro, lead.history ? getHistoryPrompt(lead) : '', mainQuestion]; return promptParts.filter(Boolean).join('\n');` This makes the system more modular and easier to test.
tasks.testStrategy: Update unit tests for `prompt-manager.ts`. Add new test cases that verify the conditional logic. For instance, test prompt generation with and without lead history to ensure the output is correct in both scenarios.

tasks.title: Extend AI Response Validation and Scoring System
tasks.description: Extend the current AI response scoring system to include more nuanced validation checks, such as checking for specific keywords, sentiment analysis, or adherence to a predefined format.
tasks.details: In the AI response validation utility, add new functions that perform more advanced checks. For sentiment, a lightweight library like 'sentiment' could be used. For format adherence, use regular expressions or JSON schema validation if the AI is expected to return structured data. Update the overall scoring algorithm to weigh these new checks appropriately.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests for each new validation function. Provide mock AI responses that should pass and fail each specific check. Test the overall scoring function to ensure the weights are applied correctly and the final score is as expected.

tasks.title: Integrate Few-Shot Examples from Database into Prompts
tasks.description: Implement logic to fetch and dynamically integrate few-shot examples from the Supabase database into the AI prompt, enhancing the AI's contextual understanding and response quality.
tasks.details: 1. Create a new RPC in Supabase, `get_prompt_examples(topic TEXT)`, that efficiently retrieves relevant examples. 2. In the frontend, before calling `prompt-manager.ts`, fetch these examples using the Supabase client. 3. Pass the fetched examples to the prompt construction function. 4. The prompt manager will then format these examples correctly (e.g., `User: ...\nAI: ...`) and insert them into the appropriate section of the main prompt.
tasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test that mocks the Supabase RPC call. Verify that the `prompt-manager` correctly incorporates the mock examples into the final prompt string. Manually test the end-to-end flow to ensure examples are fetched and used correctly, leading to improved AI responses.

tasks.title: Develop a Variable Interpolation Template Engine
tasks.description: Develop a simple but effective template engine for messaging that supports variable interpolation, allowing users to create message templates with placeholders like {{lead_name}}.
tasks.details: Create a utility function `interpolateTemplate(template: string, data: object): string`. This function will use a regular expression like `/\{\{\s*(\w+)\s*\}\}/g` to find placeholders. It will then replace each placeholder with the corresponding value from the `data` object. Example: `interpolateTemplate('Hello {{name}}', { name: 'John' })` should return `'Hello John'`. This avoids adding a heavy dependency like Handlebars for a simple use case.
tasks.testStrategy: Create a unit test file for the template engine utility. Test with various inputs: a template with multiple variables, a template with no variables, a template with variables not present in the data object (should not replace them), and edge cases like empty strings.

tasks.title: Implement Enhanced Lead Scoring Algorithm
tasks.description: Design and implement an enhanced lead scoring algorithm that goes beyond basic qualification, incorporating factors from conversation analysis, AI response scores, and lead engagement.
tasks.details: Create a new Supabase RPC `calculate_lead_score(lead_id UUID)`. This function will aggregate data for a given lead: number of messages, AI conversation phase, sentiment scores from AI validation, and lead profile data. It will apply a weighted formula to these factors to produce a numerical score. The frontend will call this RPC to display the score on the lead's profile.
tasks.testStrategy: Test the Supabase RPC directly using the Supabase SQL editor or a testing framework like `pg_prove`. Create mock leads with different characteristics and verify that the calculated score matches expectations. On the frontend, test that the score is fetched and displayed correctly.

tasks.title: Create Advanced Analytics and Reporting Dashboard
tasks.description: Build a new dashboard page for conversation insights and reporting, displaying key metrics like average response time, lead qualification rate, and AI performance.
tasks.details: 1. Create a new lazy-loaded page component `AnalyticsPage.tsx`. 2. Develop several new Supabase RPCs to aggregate analytics data efficiently (e.g., `get_analytics_summary(date_range)`, `get_ai_performance_stats()`). 3. Use a charting library like `recharts` or `chart.js` (with `react-chartjs-2`) to visualize the data. 4. Display key metrics in cards and use charts for trends over time. Leverage TanStack Query to cache the analytics data.
tasks.testStrategy: On the backend, test the RPCs to ensure they return accurate aggregations. On the frontend, use RTL to render the analytics page with mock data and assert that the key metrics are displayed. Manually verify that charts render correctly and are interactive.

tasks.title: Implement Lead/Conversation Data Export and Import
tasks.description: Implement functionality for users to export lead and conversation data to CSV and import leads from a CSV file.
tasks.details: Export: Create a utility function that takes an array of lead/conversation objects and converts them to a CSV string. Use a library like `papaparse` for robust CSV generation. Trigger a file download from the browser. Import: Use `papaparse` to parse an uploaded CSV file in the browser. Provide a mapping UI for users to match CSV columns to lead fields. Create a Supabase RPC for bulk-inserting the parsed lead data.
tasks.testStrategy: Export: Write a unit test to verify the CSV string output is correct for a given JSON input. Manually test the download functionality. Import: Test the CSV parsing logic with various valid and malformed CSV files. Write an integration test for the bulk-insert RPC to ensure data integrity and error handling.

tasks.title: Refactor for AI Model Flexibility (Multi-Provider Support)
tasks.description: Refactor the AI integration layer to support multiple AI providers beyond Google Gemini, allowing for model flexibility and future expansion.
tasks.details: Create an abstract `AIProvider` interface or class with a standard method signature, e.g., `generateResponse(prompt, options)`. Implement a `GeminiProvider` that conforms to this interface. Refactor the existing AI call sites to use a factory function `getAIProvider(providerName)` which returns the appropriate provider instance. This isolates provider-specific logic and makes adding new providers (e.g., OpenAI) as simple as creating a new class that implements the `AIProvider` interface.
tasks.testStrategy: Ensure all existing AI-related tests pass after the refactor. Create a new test suite for the provider factory and the `GeminiProvider` to ensure they work correctly. If possible, create a mock `TestProvider` to verify that the abstraction works as intended without making real API calls.
